newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Great Eastern Life gets Indonesia JV deal.
newsitem.headline: Great Eastern Life gets Indonesia JV deal.

text.p: Singapore's Great Eastern Life Assurance Co Ltd, said on Monday it was expanding into Indonesia after winning a licence from the country's authorities to run a new joint venture life insurer.
Tan Beng Lee, Great Eastern chief executive, said in a statement the move was "in line with our long-term intention to enter into other regional markets".
The company has operations in both Singapore and Malaysia.
Great Eastern said its Indonesian partner was PT Asuransi Jiwa Bumi Asih Jaya and the joint venture would be capitalised at Rupiah 10 billion (Singapore $6 million).

The statement said a controlling 55 percent stake in the company, called PT Asuransi Jiwa Asih Great Eastern, was held by Great Eastern, 24.75 percent by PT Asuransi, and the balance by minority shareholders.
The joint venture would provide financial services, plans for protection, savings, investment and insurance-based products, the statement said.
Tan said there was a "large potential market for life insurance as only eight percent of the population has life insurance".
Great Eastern expects the market penetration to grow in line with Indonesia's continuing economic expansion.
